headline: AI lab Odyssey has released Odyssey-3, a single 'world model' it says can steer robot arms, humanoids, a car and drones.
score_reason: New release with broad claims; facts match the article, but the results are the company's own.
importance_line: Robotics and self-driving developers could one day start from one general model instead of building a separate system for each machine, but this is a research preview, the demonstrations are the company's own and no independent testing is reported.
summary: The Next Web reports that Odyssey, a Palo Alto AI lab, launched a research preview of Odyssey-3, a world model (an AI that learns from video to predict how a scene will change) that the company says drove a car on real roads in India with a driving policy trained on about 20 hours of data. Odyssey says it scored 66.1 on a physics-video test, the highest reported on that leaderboard, and ranked first in three of four categories of another benchmark; both results are the company's own.
notes: Read The Next Web in full. Car, robot-arm, humanoid and drone demonstrations are claimed by Odyssey.
